info.title: Internship | Retail Network
info.jobDescription:
The opportunity

We're currently looking for an Intern - ideally starting as soon as possible for minimum duration of 6 months on a full-time basis. Someone to join our Retail Network team in order to manage and grow Polestar’s retail and dealer network in Germany. Someone with a passion for electric and sustainable mobility, an interest in technology, and a desire to create and shape the change we know is needed. And someone who doesn't mind the occasional bit of sustainable travel across Germany in the service of a cleaner form of electric performance.

This position is located at our Cologne office requiring a minimum of three days per week. We believe in a hybrid model when it comes to remote and onsite work, knowing that both in-person collaboration and individual time to focus are needed. What matters most is that people get the time, and support, to do what needs to be done. And to enjoy doing it, of course.

 

The responsibilities

In this role, you'll be expected to support the network development team. Working as a member of the Retail Network team you'll be instrumental in delivering Polestar’s dealer network growth, network strategy and project execution. See below for a more thorough breakdown of the various tasks and areas you'll be responsible for:

  • Supporting the network development process for Polestar Germany in close collaboration with Polestar HQ in Sweden

  • Support network development projects ranging from network strategy, partner acquisition, location selection, site visits, location planning and execution

  • Establish and ensure retail standards and operational guidelines across all Polestar locations

  • Provide continuous market analyses

  • Preparation of presentations with direct visibility to the Polestar executive team.

 

The ideal candidate

In order to succeed in this role, and at Polestar in general, there are a few characteristics you'll need to have. Tenacity. Flexibility. Curiosity. The ability to take the initiative, to meet deadlines and requirements, and to abandon ideas when they're not feasible.

  • Passionate with a strong and self-driven work ethic

  • Communicator, as it is important for managing our external partners and sites

  • Structured as we are a fast paced business

  • Hands-on & solution oriented.

In addition, you'll need the following qualifications:

  • Fluent in German & English (min. C1 written and spoken), main communication will be in German

  • Driver’s license (Klasse B)

  • MS Office (Excel, PPT, Teams, Outlook, etc.)

  • Enrolled in a Bachelor's or Master's degree programme for the entire duration of the internship (ideally 3rd semester or later for Bachelor's)

  • Business, finance and/or automotive studies as a basis desired

  • Ideally 1 or 2 previous internships. However, not having completed an internship is not disqualifying.

Polestar is an international company, with various backgrounds represented. And though we have a global presence, we maintain the growth-mindset. Change happens often at Polestar. But so does progress. Expect an accelerating, exciting environment.

 

The process

If the above matches your ambitions, be sure to apply. Our selection process is ongoing, and the job advert will remain open until it’s filled.

The Polestar journey is an electric one.

info.title: Senior Customs Operations Specialist
info.jobDescription:
The opportunity

We are looking for a Senior Customs Operations Specialist to join Polestar’s Global Customs team within the Quality & Logistics organization.

As Polestar continues to expand globally, Customs has become a strategic business area that supports market growth, manufacturing expansion, supply chain resilience, and operational excellence across our international operations.

This is an opportunity to join a highly visible global function working at the intersection of logistics, manufacturing, procurement, finance, commercial operations, and legal compliance. Every vehicle launch, new market entry, manufacturing footprint, and cross-border supply chain flow relies on robust customs processes that enable growth while ensuring compliance.

Let us describe the challenge we offer

This role is not simply about compliance. It is about enabling business success in an increasingly complex international trade environment.

As a Senior Customs Operations Specialist, you will support strategic initiatives ranging from vehicle launches and manufacturing expansion to customs optimization and process development. You will play an important role in ensuring efficient customs operations, supporting compliance, and contributing to business decisions that impact Polestar’s operational performance and future growth.

This role is located at: Gothenburg, Sweden.

What you’ll do

As a Senior Customs Operations Specialist, you will act as a key customs specialist supporting international trade activities across the organization. You will work closely with internal stakeholders and external customs service providers to ensure compliant, efficient, and reliable customs operations throughout the supply chain.

You will contribute to both operational and improvement-focused initiatives while helping maintain high standards of customs governance and compliance.

This includes:

  • Providing guidance on customs classification, valuation, origin determination, and import/export compliance.

  • Supporting new vehicle launches, manufacturing footprints, logistics flows, and market expansion initiatives from a customs perspective.

  • Ensuring compliance with customs regulations and trade requirements across Polestar’s global operations.

  • Identifying, assessing, and mitigating customs-related compliance, operational, and financial risks.

  • Supporting continuous improvements in customs processes, governance, and internal controls.

  • Assisting with customs audits, compliance reviews, and interactions with customs authorities.

  • Supporting the development and maintenance of customs policies, standards, and best practices.

  • Identifying opportunities for duty optimization through free trade agreements and special customs procedures.

  • Collaborating with customs brokers, logistics providers, and authorities to ensure efficient cross-border operations.

  • Delivering customs training and awareness activities across the business.

  • Monitoring regulatory developments and translating requirements into practical business solutions.

  • Supporting the continued development of Polestar’s global customs capability and long-term strategy.

Who you are

We believe you are an experienced customs professional who combines strong technical expertise with a commercial and operational mindset. You are comfortable working across organizational boundaries, collaborating with stakeholders, and translating complex regulations into practical business solutions.

You enjoy solving complex challenges, driving improvements, and making a measurable impact on business performance in an international environment.

You bring:

  • Experience within customs, international trade, trade compliance, or customs operations.

  • Good knowledge of customs regulations, customs valuation, tariff classification, origin determination, and import/export requirements.

  • Experience supporting international supply chains and cross-border operations.

  • Experience working with customs authorities, customs brokers, and logistics service providers.

  • Understanding of customs risk management and compliance frameworks.

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.

  • Strong communication and stakeholder management capabilities.

  • Fluency in English, written and spoken.

In addition you:

Have experience in one or more of the following areas:

  • Automotive industry.

  • Manufacturing operations.

  • Authorized Economic Operator (AEO) programmes.

  • Customs audits and governmental reviews.

  • Multi-regional customs operations.

  • Free Trade Agreements and customs optimization programmes.

  • Export control regulations, sanctions screening, and broader trade compliance programmes.

People at Polestar

We know that change is needed. We also know that each one of us can help bring about that change. Our commitment to becoming climate-neutral by 2040 is just as important to us as being inclusive, diverse, and innovative. Together, we are creating, collaborating, and experimenting to usher in a new era of sustainable mobility.

We are an electric performance brand, determined to improve the society we live in.

Is this you?

If you are interested in joining the Polestar team, we encourage you to apply as soon as possible. We apply continuous selection and may close the application process once a suitable candidate has been identified.

To support a fair, objective, and competency-based selection process, candidates will complete work-related psychometric assessments as part of the recruitment journey.

Are you ready for the journey? Which is electric, by the way…

info.title: Team Lead, Group Consolidation
info.jobDescription:
The opportunity

We’re currently looking for a Team Lead, Group Consolidation to join our Group Accounting team in Gothenburg. In this role, you will be responsible for the consolidation of global financial reporting and for providing accurate, timely and uniform consolidated financial data for Polestar Group. You will lead the group closing and reporting process, act as a trusted advisor in matters related to accounting and reporting, and play a key role in the delivery of consolidated reporting and SEC filings to Nasdaq in New York.

As a people manager, you will lead a team of five and balance operational excellence with coaching and collaboration in a global finance environment.

This position is based in Gothenburg, Sweden. We believe in a hybrid way of working that supports both focused individual work and in person collaboration, enabling teams to perform at their best.

The responsibilities

In this role, you will be expected to lead and secure accurate and timely group closings and reporting at consolidated level. Working as part of Group Accounting, you will be instrumental in ensuring high quality financial reporting and analysis across the group.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Leading the monthly, quarterly and yearly group closing process, including group consolidation and internal and external financial reporting

  • Performing financial analysis on group level

  • Preparing external IFRS quarterly and annual financial reports

  • Providing accounting guidance to the wider finance organisation

  • Participating in finance related projects and initiatives

The ideal candidate

To succeed in this role and at Polestar, you need to be confident in navigating complex accounting topics, comfortable working under tight deadlines, and able to combine leadership with hands on expertise. You have experience taking a leading role in a team setting and are used to collaborating across functions and with external stakeholders. You communicate clearly, can provide guidance when needed, and are comfortable acting as a speaking partner on accounting and reporting matters in an international environment.

In addition, you’ll need the following qualifications:

  • A university degree in Business Administration with a focus on finance or accounting, which provides the technical foundation required for group accounting and consolidation work

  • Minimum ten years of relevant experience from a global corporate accounting function or audit environment, enabling you to manage complex group reporting requirements

  • Strong knowledge of IFRS accounting standards and group consolidation, essential for accurate external and internal reporting

  • Experience from leading or coaching a team, which is required to succeed as a people manager

  • Solid experience working with consolidation systems, primarily AARO, used in the group consolidation process

English is the language of written and spoken communication at Polestar. We are an international company with a strong growth mindset, operating in a fast moving environment where change is common and progress is continuous.

The process

If this sounds like a match for your ambitions, we look forward to hearing from you. We apply continuous selection and may close the application process once a suitable candidate has been identified.

As part of our recruitment process, you will complete work-related psychometric assessments. These assessments are designed to support an objective and fair evaluation of the competencies, skills, and potential required for success in the role.

info.title: Product Cybersecurity Engineer
info.jobDescription:
The opportunity

We're looking for a Product Cybersecurity Engineer to help ensure that Polestar's products meet global cybersecurity standards and regulatory requirements throughout the vehicle lifecycle. In this role, you will work across concept, development, production, and post-launch operations, contributing to the implementation and validation of cybersecurity requirements that help safeguard our vehicle systems.

Let us describe the challenge we offer

As a Product Cybersecurity Engineer, you will play a key role in defining, integrating, and verifying technical security controls across our products. Working closely with R&D, suppliers, and cross-functional teams, you will support secure product development through threat analysis, secure design, cybersecurity validation, and regulatory compliance activities.

This role is located at our HQ in Gothenburg, Sweden.

What you'll do

You will be responsible for implementing and validating cybersecurity requirements across the vehicle lifecycle while supporting compliance with standards and regulations such as ISO/SAE 21434 and UNECE R155.

This includes:

  • Define, decompose, trace, and maintain product cybersecurity requirements and assurance cases.

  • Perform and/or support Threat Analysis and Risk Assessments (TARA) and risk treatment activities.

  • Plan and execute cybersecurity validation and verification activities, including testing and reviews.

  • Review supplier cybersecurity work products and support the closure of identified findings.

  • Support the generation of technical evidence required for regulatory audits and type approvals.

  • Collaborate with system architects, software and hardware teams, and functional safety teams to ensure secure integration.

  • Contribute to the continuous improvement of security engineering methods, tools, and templates.

Who you are

You are an experienced cybersecurity engineer with a strong background in product or embedded cybersecurity. You enjoy working collaboratively across disciplines and are comfortable balancing technical depth with regulatory and compliance requirements.

You bring:

  • A minimum of 5 years of experience in product or embedded cybersecurity engineering.

  • Strong knowledge of ISO/SAE 21434, UNECE R155, and secure development lifecycle practices.

  • Proficiency in TARA methodologies, security requirements engineering, and validation and verification techniques.

  • Hands-on experience with security testing tools such as CAN analyzers, fuzzers, and penetration testing frameworks.

  • A degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Cybersecurity, or a related field.

  • Relevant cybersecurity certifications, are considered a plus.

People at Polestar

We know that change is needed. We also know that each one of us can help bring about that change. Our commitment to becoming climate-neutral by 2040 is just as important to us as being inclusive, diverse, and innovative. Together, we are creating, collaborating, and experimenting to usher in a new era of sustainable mobility.

We are an electric performance brand, determined to improve the society we live in.

Is this you?

info.title: Internal Fleet Coordinator
info.jobDescription:
Let us describe the opportunity we offer

At Polestar, we believe that the transition to sustainable mobility is not just about the cars we build, but also about how we manage, deploy and optimise them.

We are currently looking for an experienced Internal Fleet Coordinator for Belgium & Luxembourg. In this key role, you will be responsible for the operational and strategic management of our internal fleet of approximately 150 vehicles, with an annual turnover of 3 to 4 replacement cycles.

Based in the Remarketing Department, you will work closely daily with Sales, Marketing, PR, Events, Finance, Operations and external partners. This gives you a unique position within the organisation, with a direct impact on cost control, vehicle availability and the Polestar customer experience.

What you’ll do

Fleet & Car Park Management

· Management of a balanced car park structure (In Fleet, Active Fleet and Display Fleet).

· Overseeing the deployment of demonstration, job and service vehicles in accordance with internal guidelines.

· Managing vehicle inflows and outflows based on age, mileage and business needs.

· Organising and monitoring periodic fleet inventories.

Vehicle Lifecycle Management

· End-to-end coordination of vehicles throughout their entire lifecycle.

· Managing administration, registration, insurance and documentation.

· Monitoring of vehicle statuses, maintenance, damage, recalls and fines.

· Proactively preventing operational disruptions and downtime.

Planning & Vehicle Availability

· Centralised planning of test vehicles, events, vehicle changes, maintenance and transport.

· Maximising vehicle availability and utilisation rates.

· Coordination with internal stakeholders regarding fleet requirements.

· Coordination of transport and logistics movements.

Stakeholder & Compliance Management

· Monitoring fleet processes and internal compliance.

· Central point of contact for internal departments and external suppliers.

· Ensuring correct vehicle check-in and check-out procedures.

· Compliance with contractual agreements and internal policies.

Supplier & Cost Management

· Managing and evaluating external partners and suppliers.

· Monitoring SLAs, quality and invoicing.

· Continuously seeking optimisations in terms of costs, efficiency and processes.

Your profile

· At least 3 to 5 years’ experience in fleet management or automotive operations.

· Strong organisational skills and excellent process monitoring.

· Experience dealing with various stakeholders and suppliers.

· You are proactive and take ownership.

· Good knowledge of Dutch and English. French is a strong asset.

· Strong analytical skills with an eye for detail and cost control.

People at Polestar

We know change is needed — and we believe every one of us can contribute to that change. Our commitment to becoming climate‑neutral by 2040 is as important as building an inclusive, diverse and innovative workplace.
Together, we are creating, collaborating and experimenting as we shape the future of sustainable mobility.

We are an electric performance brand, determined to improve the society we live in.

Is this you?

info.title: Head of Financial Planning & Analysis
info.jobDescription:
The opportunity

We are looking for a Head of Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A), to lead our financial planning, performance analysis and reporting functions. In this role, you will act as a strategic partner to the business and executive leadership team, providing forward-looking insights, enabling data-driven decision-making and supporting the achievement of our financial and sustainability goals.

Let us describe the challenge we offer

As Head of FP&A, you will play a key role in driving financial performance across the organization. You will lead financial planning, forecasting and reporting while ensuring the business has the insights, tools and processes needed to make informed decisions in a dynamic environment.

This role is located at: Gothenburg, Sweden

What you’ll do

You will lead the organization’s financial planning and analysis activities, ensuring alignment between financial performance and strategic priorities. Working closely with executive leadership, business units and functional leaders, you will provide actionable insights and guidance to support business growth, operational efficiency and profitability.

This includes:

  • Leading the annual budgeting process, ensuring alignment with strategic priorities and organizational goals.

  • Driving rolling forecasts to provide up-to-date financial projections that reflect changes in market conditions, business priorities and other key variables.

  • Leading scenario planning, sensitivity analysis and risk and opportunity assessments to support risk management and investment decisions.

  • Delivering timely, accurate and insightful financial reports, including key performance indicators and variance analysis against budget and forecast, together with actionable recommendations.

  • Preparing and presenting financial reports to senior management, the Board and other key stakeholders.

  • Managing group-wide cash flow planning and forecasting to ensure sufficient liquidity for operational and strategic needs.

  • Collaborating with business units and functional leaders to align financial plans with corporate objectives.

  • Driving initiatives that improve operational efficiency and profitability across the organization.

  • Continuously improving planning, forecasting and reporting processes to increase efficiency and accuracy.

  • Partnering with Digital/IT to implement and optimize financial systems supporting forecasting, reporting and analytics.

  • Driving automation and standardization initiatives across FP&A processes.

  • Fostering a culture of accountability, continuous improvement and innovation within the finance organization.

Who you are

You are a collaborative and business-minded finance leader with extensive experience in financial planning, reporting and controlling. You combine strong analytical capabilities with the ability to communicate complex financial information in a clear and actionable way. You are comfortable operating in an international environment and thrive in a fast-moving organization where teamwork and business impact come first.

You bring:

  • 10+ years of experience in a finance leadership role within the automotive industry.

  • A bachelor's or master's degree in Finance, or equivalent experience demonstrating exceptional ability.

  • International work experience is highly desirable.

  • Strong business acumen.

  • A controlling background with knowledge of IFRS, US GAAP, local GAAP, local reporting requirements and regulations.

  • A data-driven approach with the ability to identify business opportunities and risks through analysis.

  • Strong experience with business analytics tools.

  • The ability to communicate financial analysis, forecasting, budgeting and internal controls effectively to business stakeholders.

  • Experience with modern leadership practices and the ability to lead both independently and through others while navigating cultural differences.

  • Strong prioritization skills across your own responsibilities, your team and key deliverables to best support business objectives.

In addition, you:

  • Demonstrate strong leadership skills and personal drive.

  • Have excellent analytical and structured ways of working.

  • Are flexible, proactive and pragmatic in your approach.

  • Are a strong communicator with well-developed social and relationship-building skills.

  • Bring a strong business mindset and the ability to adapt to different cultures and ways of working.

  • Believe in a non-hierarchical culture built on interaction, transparency and trust.

  • Prioritize actions that are best for the organization and its long-term success.

  • Have a passion for collaboration and thrive in an evolving, flat work culture that values collective success over individual gains.

People at Polestar

info.jobDescription:

We are looking for a passionate, experienced and a self-steering professional who can identify key opportunities within the small and medium-sized enterprises segment. A key part of your responsibility is managing the back office topics ensuring to maintain the high-quality service expected for our clients.

This position is located at our office in Vienna. We believe in a hybrid model when it comes to remote and onsite work, knowing that both in-person collaboration and individual time to focus are needed. What matters most is that people get the time, and support, to do what needs to be done. And to enjoy doing it, of course.

In this role you will take over responsibility on process flows and control the flow of payments from Polestar to partners but also the payments from our partners. In the POD (Planning, Order & Delivery) team you will have the possibility to be part of the whole sales process – both for new and pre-owned Polestar cars.   • Ensure that all payments are under control und processed in time

  • Reports on market registrations and detailed analysis of segments and market trends

info.title: Manager Fleet Sales
info.jobDescription:
The opportunity

We have an exciting opportunity at Polestar for someone who thrives in a fast-paced, exciting, and dynamic organisation. As one of the key European markets, we are now seeking a Manager Fleet Sales to join the Polestar Netherlands team, reporting directly to the Head of Sales.

This is a key role in the business and you will be responsible for leading the Fleet Sales team and developing and implementing the local Fleet Sales strategy. You will own the commercial relationships with all major leasing companies in the Netherlands and play a pivotal role in growing Polestar’s presence and performance within the corporate and fleet market.

You will lead a team of six FTE and be responsible for building strong, long-term relationships with fleet customers, SME customers and leasing partners. This includes managing complex tender processes, negotiating and managing local framework agreements, and ensuring that Polestar maximises its commercial opportunities across the fleet channel.

Therefore, we are looking for an experienced automotive sales professional with a strong understanding of the Dutch fleet and leasing landscape. You are commercially astute, results-driven and highly collaborative, with a proven ability to navigate complex stakeholder environments and turn strategic opportunities into tangible business results.

 

The responsibilities

Working with colleagues across Polestar Netherlands and the wider Polestar organisation, the key responsibilities of the Manager Fleet Sales role are to deliver the fleet sales objectives and optimise Polestar’s performance across the corporate and leasing channel:

  • Develop and implement the local Fleet Sales strategy, aligned with Polestar Netherlands’ overall commercial objectives.

  • Lead, manage and develop the Fleet Sales team of six FTE, ensuring clear objectives, strong performance and continuous professional development.

  • Own and manage the strategic relationships with all major leasing companies in the Netherlands.

  • Develop and execute customer strategies for fleet customers, SME customers, leasing partners and retail partners, maximising sales potential and long-term commercial value.

  • Identify and pursue new fleet sales opportunities and partnerships within the Dutch corporate and leasing market.

  • Lead and coordinate complex tender and procurement processes ensuring Polestar is positioned competitively and that all internal and external stakeholders are effectively managed throughout the process.

  • Initiate, negotiate, renew and manage local framework agreements with key customers and partners.

  • Ensure effective contract management throughout the lifecycle of local commercial agreements, including monitoring performance, obligations and commercial opportunities.

  • Work closely with internal stakeholders (both locally and with Polestar HQ) to ensure that fleet propositions, pricing, products and commercial programmes meet the requirements of the Dutch market.

  • Monitor fleet sales performance against weekly, monthly, quarterly and annual targets and proactively report to the Management Team. Where needed, you should be able to identify opportunities to address under-performance and to support commercial decision making

  • Contribute to the development and delivery of Polestar’s sales and marketing activities within the fleet and corporate channel.

  • Represent Polestar at relevant industry forums, customer events and other fleet-related activities, including delivering presentations.

  • Ensure a high level of customer service and professional relationship management across the fleet channel.

 

The ideal candidate

Our ideal candidate has a comprehensive understanding of- and experience in working with the following:

  • Fleet and leasing sales within the automotive industry

  • The Dutch fleet and leasing market and its key stakeholders

  • Strategic account management and relationship development

  • Tender and procurement processes, including complex and multi-stakeholder tenders

  • Contract management and negotiation

  • Local framework agreements and commercial partnerships

  • Sales strategy development and execution

  • Whole Life Cost Management

  • Sound product knowledge, in particular of EVs

  • Relationship dynamics – the ability to influence and direct the actions of others, both internally and externally, in order to secure optimal business performance

  • Sales performance management, forecasting and commercial analysis

  • Digital tools as Salesforce CRM, the full MS Office suite and other PS developed applications

In addition, you'll need the following qualifications:

  • HBO or University degree

  • At least 7 years of experience as an automotive sales professional with significant experience within fleet, leasing and/or corporate sales

  • Proven experience in managing strategic relationships with major leasing companies with strong negotiation and influencing skills

  • Demonstrable experience in leading and developing a sales team

  • Experience in managing complex tender and procurement processes

  • Strong experience in contract negotiation and management, including local framework agreements

  • Excellent written and oral communication skills in both Dutch and English

  • Highly collaborative, proactive and skilled at building strong relationships

  • Digitally savvy, with a strong understanding of modern sales technologies, CRM systems and data-driven decision making

Polestar is an international company, with various nationalities represented. English, therefore, is the language of written and spoken communication. And though we have a global presence, we maintain the start-up mentality that saw us grow so rapidly. Expect a fast-paced, exciting environment. Change happens often at Polestar. But so does progress.

 

About us

We are an electric performance car brand, determined to improve the society we live in. Our focus is on uncompromised design and technology. Passion and emotion drive us, electricity and innovation drive our cars. Our products are excellent, efficient and entertaining.

In Polestar’s future, there is no room for shortcuts, excuses or compromises. We are all in, dedicated on our ambition. Guiding our industry forward through pure, progressive, performance.

If you want to join us and play a pivotal role in shaping the future of Fleet Sales at Polestar Netherlands, please apply.

info.title: HR Projects Admin (Fixed-Term Contract- 6 Months)
info.jobDescription:
The opportunity

We're currently looking for an HR Projects (FTC- 6 Months) to join our HR Business Commercial team and help us deliver agile and reliable HR support across the UK Sales Unit. This role is primarily focused on supporting a key HR data and systems project, ensuring employee data is accurate, complete and up to date within our HRIS and Employee Communication portal. The role will also provide HR administrative support and assist with wider HR activities as required. If you're passionate about attention to detail, data accuracy, continuous improvement and creating efficient HR processes, this is your chance to make an impact in a fast-moving, innovative environment.

You'll be part of the HR Business Commercial team and report to the HR Business Partner UK. The role is based in Bicester, UK. We recognize the value of in-person collaboration and have a 3 days a week in the office policy, but what matters most is having the time, tools and trust to get things done and to enjoy doing them.

Please note that this is a six-month fixed-term position and, internally, the role will be known as HR Trainee. The role has been created to support a number of HR projects and organisational improvement initiatives during a period of increased business activity. This is a temporary position established to meet a specific business requirement and is therefore expected to end upon completion of the six-month fixed-term contract.

The responsibilities

As an HR Projects Officer, you will play a key role in supporting critical HR system and data management activities, with a primary focus on ensuring employee data within our HRIS and employee communication portable is accurate, up to date, complete and maintained to a high standard. Working closely with the HR Business Partner UK, you will support HR projects, maintain data integrity, provide HR administrative support and assist with a variety of people-related activities across the business.

Key Responsibilities

• Maintain, validate and cleanse employee data within our HRIS, ensuring accuracy, completeness and data integrity.

• Drive the transfer and maintenance of employee data and documentation within our HRIS, ensuring all employee lifecycle records and documentation are captured and stored appropriately.

• Review and optimise employee lifecycle processes within our HRIS, ensuring workflows remain effective, compliant and fit for purpose.

• Maintain and update employee-facing HR information and communication portal, ensuring content remains relevant, accurate and accessible.

• Produce HR reports, metrics and data analysis from the HRIS to support HR and business decision-making.

• Support HR audits, compliance activities and governance requirements through effective record management and data controls.

• Work closely with managers and stakeholders to ensure employee information is maintained accurately and consistently across HR systems.

• Build effective working relationships across the business and contribute to continuous improvement initiatives.

• Provide ad hoc HR administration and operational support across the HR team as required.

About You

To be successful in this role, you will be highly organised, detail-oriented and comfortable working with large volumes of employee data. You will enjoy problem-solving, have excellent attention to detail and be confident working with HR systems and multiple stakeholders. You will also be flexible and willing to support broader HR activities when required.

Skills, Experience & Qualifications

• Previous experience in an HR Administration, HR Coordinator, HR Projects or similar support role.

• Experience maintaining employee data and working with HR systems.

• Strong understanding of HR administration and employee lifecycle processes.

• Experience using Workday is highly desirable.

• Candidates without Workday experience must have experience using another HR Information System (HRIS).

• Experience working with employee data, reporting and data accuracy initiatives.

• Strong IT skills, particularly Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint and Microsoft Office applications.

• Exceptional attention to detail and accuracy, combined with a proactive mindset and a commitment to delivering high-quality outcomes.

info.title: Information Security Coordinator
info.jobDescription:
The opportunity

Following recent K-ISMS audit findings and the continued development of Polestar Korea’s information security, we are establishing the role of Information Security Coordinator.

As Information Security Coordinator, you will act as the designated coordination point between Polestar Korea and Polestar HQ Security, supporting local information security governance, compliance-, audit-, and evidence coordination, stakeholder engagement, issue follow-up and escalation.

This position is located at Polestar Automotive Korea office in Gangnam-gu, Seoul. We believe in a hybrid model when it comes to remote and onsite work, knowing that both in-person collaboration and individual time to focus are needed. What matters most is that people get the time, and support, to do what needs to be done. And to enjoy doing it, of course.

Let us describe the challenge we offer

Information security relies on clear ownership, structured coordination, and close collaboration between local teams and Polestar HQ Security.

In this role, you will help ensure that Polestar Korea can coordinate and demonstrate local information security activities in a structured and documented way. You will work with local stakeholders and HQ Security Department to coordinate K-ISMS-related activities, collect and maintain evidence, follow up on actions and findings, and support audits, assessments and certification-related activities.

For work performed within the Information Security Coordinator role, priorities, governance activities, working methods, and deliverables are functionally governed by the Head of Information Security at Polestar HQ.

What you'll do

You will support the local operation of information security governance in Polestar Korea.

  • Coordinate local information security activities.

  • Support K-ISMS and other relevant information security compliance activities.

  • Coordinate information security audits, assessments, reviews and certification-related activities.

  • Coordinate collection and maintenance of information security evidence and documentation.

  • Track and follow-up actions, findings, issues, dependencies, and corrective actions.

  • Acts as the local liaison between Polestar Korea and Polestar HQ Security.

  • Support engagement with relevant local stakeholders.

  • Escalate blockers, overdue actions, unclear ownership, and material information security issues when required.

  • Provide periodic status updates to Polestar HQ Security.

 

Who you are

You are a structured and collaborative professional who enjoys coordinating activities across different stakeholders and functions. You are comfortable working with documentation, follow-up, governance, compliance and continuous improvement.

You do not need to be an information security specialist today. We believe successful candidates may come from different backgrounds where coordination, governance, compliance, controls, audit, quality, risk or process management are already part of their work.

To be a great fit for this position we believe you have:

  • Strong coordination and stakeholder management skills.

  • A structured and methodical approach to planning, documentation, and follow-up.

  • Experience from areas such as governance, compliance, quality management, internal control or audit, risk management, process management, finance controls, legal operations, HR governance, or similar disciplines.

  • Good communication skills and the ability to work with stakeholders across functions.

  • Good judgement in escalating issues, risks, blockers, or unclear ownership.

  • An interest in learning more about information security.

At Polestar, you will be part of a cross-functional and international team, with English as a natural language for written and spoken communication. Since Polestar’s in a scale-up phase you thrive by working in a fast-paced environment.

No previous information security experience?

That is perfectly fine. The Information Security Coordinator role is designed for employees with strong coordination, governance, compliance, audit, risk quality, or similar backgrounds.

Successful candidates will receive training, onboarding, and ongoing support from the Polestar HQ Security organization to develop the knowledge required to perform the role effectively.

People at Polestar

info.title: Cybersecurity Engineer
info.jobDescription:
The opportunity

Polestar is accelerating the transition to sustainable mobility through electric performance. As a digital-first, cloud-driven organisation, cybersecurity is a critical enabler of our business, products, and services.

We are looking for a Cybersecurity Engineer to strengthen and evolve our enterprise security capabilities. This role focuses on designing, implementing, operating, and continuously improving security controls that protect our workforce, data, identities, devices, networks, and digital services.

This is not a traditional operations-focused security role. We are looking for an engineer who enjoys building, automating, and improving security capabilities at scale while working closely with technology teams across the organisation.

Let us describe the challenge we offer

As a Cybersecurity Engineer, you will play a key role in strengthening Polestar’s enterprise security posture and advancing our Zero Trust journey. You will help build scalable security capabilities that protect users, devices, identities, data, and enterprise services in a modern cloud-first environment.

This role is located at: Polestar Headquarters, Gothenburg, Sweden.

We believe in empowerment and support flexible working hours and a hybrid way of working.

What you’ll do

You will work across security engineering, automation, and operational resilience, partnering with teams throughout the organisation to embed security by design and continuously improve enterprise security capabilities.

This includes:

  • Implementing and continuously improving security capabilities across endpoint, identity, network, collaboration, and data protection domains.

  • Supporting the deployment, optimisation, and governance of enterprise security platforms and controls.

  • Building and maintaining security automations that reduce manual effort and improve operational effectiveness.

  • Improving detection, response, and resilience capabilities across the enterprise environment.

  • Partnering with infrastructure, workplace, cloud, networking, and engineering teams to embed security by design.

  • Driving the implementation of Zero Trust principles, including strong identity controls, least privilege, continuous verification, and network segmentation.

  • Supporting the secure adoption of AI technologies and helping establish technical guardrails that reduce risk while enabling innovation.

  • Improving data protection and information security capabilities to ensure sensitive information is protected throughout its lifecycle.

  • Contributing to security architecture decisions and helping define future security capabilities and standards.

  • Evaluating new technologies and continuously improving security tooling, integrations, and processes.

  • Serving as a Tier 3 security engineering escalation point for complex incidents and high-priority security events.

  • Participating in a shared on-call rotation supporting our Security Operations Centre (SOC) for approximately five weeks annually.

Who you are

You are a hands-on cybersecurity engineer who enjoys solving technical security challenges and building scalable security solutions.

You combine strong security engineering expertise with a pragmatic mindset and understand how to balance security, usability, and business objectives. You are comfortable working across engineering, operations, and automation, and can translate security requirements into effective technical controls.

Most importantly, you view security tooling and processes as systems that can be engineered, automated, and continuously improved.

You bring:

  • At least 5 years of hands-on experience in cybersecurity engineering.

  • Strong technical understanding of enterprise security architectures and controls.

  • Experience implementing security solutions across endpoint, identity, network, and data protection domains.

  • Experience building automations, integrations, or custom tooling to improve security operations and engineering outcomes.

  • Strong scripting and problem-solving skills.

  • Experience working in cloud-first and modern enterprise environments.

  • Ability to collaborate effectively with both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

  • A passion for continuous improvement and a builder’s mindset.

You have experience with:

  • Microsoft security technologies.

  • Data protection, data security, privacy, and DLP.

  • Endpoint security and device management.

  • Network security and Zero Trust architectures.

  • Email and collaboration security.

  • Security automation, orchestration, and scripting.

  • Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) and secure configuration management.

In addition, you may also have experience with:

  • Identity, access, and privilege management.

  • Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) and cryptographic controls.

  • AI security, governance, and risk management.

You are motivated by creating meaningful impact and helping strengthen security capabilities across identities, endpoints, networks, and data. You enjoy increasing automation, improving resilience, expanding Zero Trust adoption, and enabling the secure and responsible use of emerging technologies, including AI.

People at Polestar

We know that change is needed. We also know that each one of us can help bring about that change. Our commitment to becoming climate-neutral by 2040 is just as important to us as being inclusive, diverse, and innovative. Together, we are creating, collaborating, and experimenting to usher in a new era of sustainable mobility. We are an electric performance brand, determined to improve the society we live in.

info.title: Corporate Legal Counsel
info.jobDescription:
The opportunity

We're currently looking for a Corporate Legal Counsel to join our Corporate Legal team. In this role, you will provide strategic legal advice and support across a broad range of corporate, governance, securities regulation, capital markets, finance, and transaction-related matters. You will play a key role in supporting Polestar's listed parent company and global corporate structure, helping ensure compliance with regulatory requirements while enabling the business to achieve its strategic objectives.

As part of the Legal function, you will work closely with executive management, the Board of Directors, and stakeholders across Finance, Treasury, Accounting, Sustainability, Investor Relations, and Corporate Communications. You will advise on governance matters, corporate transactions, capital markets activities, public company compliance, and other strategic initiatives that support Polestar's continued growth and transformation.

This position is located in HQ, Gothenburg, Sweden. We believe in a hybrid model when it comes to remote and onsite work, knowing that both in-person collaboration and individual focus time are important for success.

The responsibilities

In this role, you'll be a trusted business partner, providing practical legal advice to support strategic and operational decision-making across Polestar, while helping to maintain strong corporate governance and regulatory compliance.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Lead and support legal work relating to capital markets transactions, including debt and equity financings and other strategic corporate finance initiatives.

  • Advise on corporate governance matters relating to Polestar's listed parent company and global subsidiaries.

  • Support compliance with securities regulations, SEC requirements, and NASDAQ listing rules.

  • Advise on corporate policies, procedures, governance best practices, and compliance with market abuse and insider trading regulations.

  • Manage and coordinate external legal counsel across multiple jurisdictions, ensuring effective delivery and budget oversight.

  • Partner with senior stakeholders across the business to provide pragmatic legal advice that balances risk management with commercial objective.

The ideal candidate

To succeed in this role, you'll need excellent legal judgment, strong business acumen, and the ability to navigate complex legal matters in a fast-paced international environment. You combine technical legal expertise with a practical, solution-oriented mindset and are comfortable working independently while collaborating effectively with senior stakeholders across the organization. You thrive in a dynamic environment where priorities evolve, and you enjoy working on a diverse range of high-impact corporate and strategic matters.

In addition, you'll need the following qualifications:

  • Master degree in Law (LLM), preferably from relevant Swedish, U.S., or other European university.

  • Extensive relevant experience (approximately 7+ years), including experience from a leading law firm and in-house legal roles within a global publicly listed company.

  • Strong experience in securities regulation, disclosure requirements, capital markets transactions, corporate finance, M&A, and general corporate matters.

  • Knowledge of Swedish, U.K. and/or U.S. corporate law.

  • Experience managing external legal counsel and coordinating support across multiple jurisdictions.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English.

Beneficial, but not required:

  • Experience managing complex litigation matters, particularly in the U.S.

info.title: Group Control Assurance Specialist
info.jobDescription:
Group Control Assurance Specialist is part of Finance department, Group Accounting, and the Group Control Assurance function and partners closely with stakeholders across the organization to resolve complex control, governance, and risk-related challenges.

You will be responsible to facilitate the evolution and effectiveness of the SOX internal control framework by leading control design initiatives, challenging existing processes, evaluating significant control deficiencies, and facilitating sustainable remediation solutions. Working in a fast-paced international environment, you will leverage your expertise to influence stakeholders, guide decision-making, and improve control maturity across business functions while ensuring compliance with regulatory requirements.

The position is located at our HQ in Gothenburg, Sweden. We believe in empowerment and support flexible working hours and the possibility to work from home a couple of days per week.

What you'll do

You will lead the continuous enhancement of Polestar's SOX internal control environment by applying advanced professional judgment to complex control matters, driving organizational improvements, and partnering with stakeholders across the business to strengthen risk management and governance practices.

You will:

  • Lead the development and continuous enhancement of risk and control matrices, process documentation, and control frameworks by identifying underlying risks, challenging existing control environments, and driving the implementation of effective and sustainable control solutions.

  • Design and drive the implementation of new controls and control improvement initiatives, partnering with process and control owners to establish practical solutions that address business risks while supporting operational objectives.

  • Facilitate the management testing program by defining testing strategies, ensuring high-quality execution, and driving timely completion across the organization.

  • Evaluate control deficiencies, perform severity assessments, and provide expert analysis on business, financial reporting, and compliance impacts while facilitating stakeholder alignment on remediation priorities.

  • Facilitate the remediation of control deficiencies, significant deficiencies, and material weaknesses by influencing stakeholders, challenging root causes, and monitoring the implementation of sustainable corrective actions.

  • Serve as a trusted advisor to the organization by delivering specialized training, workshops, and guidance on internal controls, risk mitigation, governance practices, and remediation activities, including matters related to material weaknesses.

  • Identify and lead cross-functional improvement initiatives that enhance the efficiency, effectiveness, and maturity of internal control, governance, and assurance processes across the organization.

  • Build strong relationships and collaborate with senior stakeholders, auditors, consultants, and business leaders to resolve complex issues and support the ongoing development of Polestar's control environment.

Who you are

You are a highly analytical and proactive professional with substantial experience in internal control, risk management, and assurance within complex and regulated environments. You are comfortable navigating ambiguity, solving complex challenges, communicating with stakeholders at all organizational levels, and contributing to a growing, fast‑paced organization.

You combine technical expertise with strong business acumen and are capable of independently assessing complex situations, developing practical solutions, and facilitating organizational change.

To be a great fit for this position, we believe you have:

  • 5+ years of experience in internal control, SOX, SEC reporting requirements within a U.S. - listed company environment, risk advisory, assurance, or related areas, ideally gained through a combination of industry and/or Big Four experience.

  • Experience working in multinational organizations.

  • Deep knowledge of risk assessment, process and system scoping, control design, implementation, testing, and control remediation.

  • Experience evaluating control deficiencies, including significant deficiencies and material weaknesses, and presenting conclusions to management.

  • General knowledge of group consolidation and IFRS reporting requirements.

  • Relevant certifications such as CA, CPA, ACCA, CIA, or equivalent are considered an advantage.

Polestar is an international company with colleagues representing diverse backgrounds and perspectives. English is our primary language for written and spoken communication. As we continue to grow globally, change is constant, but so is progress. Expect an accelerating, exciting environment where your work will have visible impact.

The process

info.title: Group Category Manager – Digital
info.jobDescription:

info.title: Senior Software Developer
info.jobDescription:

At Polestar Digital, we build innovative, scalable solutions that power our global platform. With real ownership, close collaboration, and global impact, you will play a key role in shaping the future of Polestar’s digital ecosystem.

You will take ownership of system architecture and technical decision‑making while working closely with Product Managers, Designers, and Operations teams to deliver reliable and impactful solutions. The role combines hands‑on development, system design, and collaboration, while also contributing to a strong engineering culture through mentoring and knowledge‑sharing.

You will write clean, well‑tested code and contribute to building systems that are robust, scalable, and maintainable. At the same time, you will stay up to date with modern development practices and emerging technologies, including evolving paradigms such as agentic AI.

What you'll do

You will design, build, and evolve scalable digital solutions that power Polestar’s global platform.

Your responsibilities include:

  • Designing and implementing high‑performance, globally scalable systems

info.jobDescription:
The opportunity

Polestar is accelerating the transition to sustainable mobility through electric performance. Behind that journey sits a powerful digital platform enabling everything from checkout and payments to order management, delivery, retail tools, and customer self‑service.

You will join a focused team working across a critical part of the customer journey, building and validating solutions that customers globally and hundreds of internal users depend on every day. With real ownership, close collaboration, and global impact, this role plays a key part in ensuring reliability, performance, and quality across Polestar’s digital ecosystem.

We are now looking for a Senior Quality Assurance Engineer to join Polestar Digital at our headquarters in Gothenburg, Sweden.

Let us describe the challenge we offer

As a Senior Quality Assurance Engineer, you will ensure the reliability, performance, and quality of customer‑facing digital products and internal platforms that support the vehicle purchasing journey.

You will work across frontend, backend, APIs, and cloud infrastructure, validating solutions and ensuring that features meet both business and technical requirements before release. Acting as a key partner to Software Engineers, Product Managers, Designers, and Operations teams, you will translate product requirements into effective test strategies and ensure that defects are identified early and resolved efficiently.

The role combines hands‑on testing, automation, and continuous improvement of quality practices, contributing to scalable and high‑quality systems used globally across markets and internal operations. You will also stay up to date with modern QA methodologies and emerging technologies, including AI‑assisted testing approaches.

What you'll do

You will ensure high‑quality delivery across Polestar’s digital platforms by validating solutions, improving test coverage, and driving continuous improvement in quality practices.

Your responsibilities include:

  • Monitoring and evaluating quality metrics and contributing to continuous improvement initiatives

In your daily work, you will collaborate closely with Software Engineers, Product Managers, Designers, Technical Leads, and Operations teams, ensuring alignment across technical and business needs while driving quality across the full development lifecycle.

Who you are

You are a structured and analytical quality professional with strong ownership and a proactive approach to ensuring high‑quality outcomes. You are comfortable working independently while collaborating closely with cross‑functional teams, and you focus on identifying and resolving issues early to enable smooth and reliable delivery.

You combine hands‑on testing expertise with a continuous improvement mindset and an interest in modern technologies shaping the future of software quality.

info.title: Public Relations & Events Manager
info.jobDescription:
At Polestar we don't just drive innovation in our cars – our entire business model is different from our competitors. We’re looking for a creative, innovative, experienced, and hands-on professional to drive and elevate Polestars brand awareness, consideration and reputation across Canada.

Let us describe the challenge we offer
As the Public Relations & Events Manager your primary focus will be on developing and executing proactive public relations and events strategies for Polestar’s products, technology and consumer facing narratives. In partnership with Communications & Marketing, you will take lead in managing media, journalists and influencer relationships, and execute PR campaigns which drive brand awareness engagement and consideration. You will also be directly responsible for creating and executing focused events in order to deliver brand and business results in alignment with market objectives.

This role will require 20-40% travel throughout Canada and reports to the Head of Marketing, Canada.

What you’ll do

· Deliver and execute PR campaigns which build and maintain positive key media relationships for the company

· Oversee product communications from launch through lifecycle management

· Support corporate financial communications, including quarterly and annual reporting, ensuring clear, consistent messaging aligned with business performance and strategy

· Act as the main PR contact for inquiries, statements, press escalations.

· Lead experiential activities and events both for the media and the general public including product launches, auto shows, demo drives, influencer and sponsorship events.

· Drive consumer facing communication efforts to increase brand awareness, consideration, reputation

· Manage Canadian PR agencies of record, Event agency(ies), as well as vendor partners, ensuring quality completion of deliverables in support of departmental goals

· Foster close collaboration with Communication & Marketing peers, supporting them as necessary

· For PR and Marketing needs, manage and oversee the fleet vehicles, asset inventory and logistics, ensuring optimal usage, availability and maintenance

· Track, monitor and report PR and event performance and KPIs, manage departmental budget

· Upkeep and maintain internal archives and asset library

· Support in ad hoc projects, events and tasks as needed

Who you are

· 7 – 10 years of experience in Public Relations or Communications

· Bachelor’s degree in communications, Journalism or related field

· Proven experience managing events, influencer programs, and external partners.

· Excellent communication skills – both written & verbal, and both in English and in French required

· Experience working for an automotive manufacturer, or a consumer PR Agency is highly desirable

· Proven track record of managing successful PR campaigns and engaging events

· Exceptional project management and multitasking abilities.

· You understand the basic technical intricacies of the automobile, or possess the desire and proficiency to learn them

· Comfortable managing budgets, timelines, and cross-functional projects.

La marque incarne une approche avant-gardiste de l’automobile :
performance, durabilité et esthétique scandinave.

  • Expérience réussie dans la vente automobile (idéalement premium, électrique ou innovante)

  • Sensibilité aux nouvelles technologies et à la mobilité électrique

info.title: Customer Engagement Advisor
info.jobDescription:
The opportunity

We're currently looking for a Customer Engagement Advisor. Someone to join our Customer Experience team and play a key role in putting our customers first, and ensuring our Customer Engagement Centre are offering finest levels of customer service. Someone with a passion for electric mobility, an interest in technology, and a desire to create the change we know is needed.

Working directly with the Contact Centre Team Leaders, our Contact Centre Manager and our Customer Engagement Centre team this role will be key in delivering a hassle-free experience for all our customers.

This position is located at our Bicester office and will require a minimum of three days in our office. We believe in a hybrid model when it comes to remote and onsite work, knowing that both in-person collaboration and individual time to focus are needed. What matters most is that people get the time and support to do what needs to be done. And to enjoy doing it, of course.


The responsibilities

In this role, you'll be expected to champion all areas of customer engagement, putting the customer first in everything you do. Working as a member of the Customer Engagement department, you'll be instrumental in our ambition to be the best in class for customer service and offer all Polestar customers the finest experience. See below for a more thorough breakdown of the various tasks and areas you'll be responsible for:

  • Handle enquiries from customers via Inbound Calls, Emails, Cases and chats

  • Outbound follow up and delivery support calls

  • Become a champion of the Polestar products to be able to give customers the best advice and support

  • First line Complaint resolution

  • Other tasks as required for the role


The ideal candidate

In order to succeed in this role, and at Polestar in general, there are a few characteristics you'll need to have. Integrity, Kindness and Commitment. The ability to take the initiative, to meet set deadlines and requirements, and to always think customer first.

As a person you have great time management, and like to work in a team environment. You are also a digital-minded, flexible and agile individual who thrives working in fast-paced and dynamic environment and who has a can-do attitude and a self-starter approach. You are able to handle a broad portfolio of tasks and are confident supporting customers directly on a one to one basis.

In addition, you'll need the following:

  • At least 6 months of experience in front line Customer Service roles

  • Previous complaints or escalations experience

  • Excellent oral and written communication in English

  • Able to work shifts across 8am to 6pm Monday to Friday. (Overtime may be available)

  • Knowledge of Salesforce is a benefit

  • Good knowledge of Excel & PowerPoint

Polestar is an international company, with various backgrounds represented. English, therefore, is the language of written and spoken communication. And though we have a global presence, we maintain the growth-mindset. Change happens often at Polestar. But so does progress. Expect an accelerating, exciting environment.


The process

If the above matches your ambitions, be sure to apply. Our selection process is ongoing, and the job advert will remain open until it’s filled.

The Polestar journey is an electric one.
